message.content: We must examine the era when Nicolaus Copernicus formulated his revolutionary theory, recognizing that the historical and political climate was profoundly shaped by the late medieval transition into early modernity. The Church held immense power over intellectual discourse, making any challenge to geocentric cosmology a dangerous act of heresy. Yet, the fragmented political landscape of Europe allowed new ideas to circulate beyond ecclesiastical control, slowly eroding traditional Ptolemaic frameworks through emerging empirical observations and shifting state allegiances
